title: Smugglers Turned Cocaine Into a Jacket
central_question: Where they hid it: Nepal's narcotics bureau found cocaine mixed with silicone and shaped into a jacket, blankets and neck pillows (2026); Manila customs found towels and duvets soaked in meth (2026); Spanish police found shipping pallets made of 1.4 tonnes of cocaine (2015). Which was the best fake?
content_notes: Tone: absurd and ironic; the joke is on the fakes (a cocaine jacket, soaked towels, pallets made of cocaine), never on a victim (none appears). Every case is a seizure by a named agency (Nepal's Narcotics Control Bureau; the Philippine Bureau of Customs with PDEA; Spanish police with the UK National Crime Agency), a settled fact; the hook states the seizure. The two women arrested in Kathmandu are arrested, not convicted: never named, drawn only as dark rim-lit silhouettes with no face (NOT A LIKENESS), and 'police say' carries the allegation that one came to collect it. No arrest was reported in the Manila case and nobody is drawn as a suspect there; the Valencia arrests appear only as a typed label. Officers, the examiner and the chemist are generic figures in plain clothing with no badge, patch, flag, agency name or insignia; no weapon; no force shown. Boxes, the container and the pallets carry no company name, logo or plate; the X-ray image is our own false-colour drawing with typed boxes, not any real system's interface; the test tube is a generic lab illustration. The evidence table, the searched room, the warehouse, the X-ray bay, the port and the lab are illustrations, not reported scenes. Every card is our own typed graphic; no dialogue or quotation card. Facts verified 2026-10-23.

lines.text: Drug smugglers turned cocaine into a jacket.
Over 4 kilos, shaped into blankets and aprons.
But drug police searched her bags. Two women arrested.
And that was not the biggest.
In Manila: towels and duvets soaked in meth.
The biggest? Shipping pallets made of cocaine.
On a tip, lab tests found the wood was cocaine.
Even the neck pillow was cocaine.

claims.text: July 2026, Kathmandu: Nepal's Narcotics Control Bureau (Nepal Police) arrested two foreign women and seized liquid cocaine mixed with silicone and prepared in the shape and size of clothes; jackets are among the items. Narration: 'Drug smugglers turned cocaine into a jacket.' Headline 'A JACKET / MADE OF COCAINE'. Label 'KATHMANDU, NEPAL · JULY 2026'.
The seizure weighed over 4 kg (The Himalayan Times 4.28 kg; Ratopati 4.258 kg; Kantipur about 4 kg). Narration: 'Over 4 kilos, ...'.

The cocaine-silicone material was shaped into blankets, mats, jackets, aprons and neck pillows, and a false bottom in a suitcase was also used. Narration: '..., shaped into blankets and aprons.' Callout 'COCAINE + SILICONE'.
The bureau said it appears to be a new method: liquid cocaine mixed with silicone and prepared in the shape and size of clothes. Callout sub 'A new method, the bureau says'.

The first woman, a 62-year-old foreign national, landed at Tribhuvan International Airport on 15 July 2026; the bureau searched her belongings in Thamel, Kathmandu, where she was arrested. Narration (gotcha): 'But drug police searched her bags.' Label 'SEARCHED IN THAMEL, KATHMANDU'. Not named; silhouette only.

A second woman, 37, who police say came to Kathmandu to collect the consignment, was also arrested. Neither woman is named on screen; both are arrested, not convicted. Narration: 'Two women arrested.' Label 'TWO WOMEN ARRESTED · NOT NAMED', sub 'Police say one came to collect it'.

Editorial rehook, true by size: the Manila shipment (15 boxes: about 28.3 kg of suspected shabu, 4.7 kg of kush and 40 soaked towels and duvets) is bigger than the Kathmandu seizure (over 4 kg). Narration: 'And that was not the biggest.'

Announced 14 September 2026: the Philippine Bureau of Customs intercepted 15 boxes from Canada declared as personal effects at a warehouse in Pasay City (Metro Manila); among them, 20 towels and 20 duvets suspected to be soaked with liquid methamphetamine; the shipment's total value was over P199.7 million, and PDEA lab tests on samples confirmed methamphetamine and cannabis. No arrest reported. Narration: 'In Manila: towels and duvets soaked in meth.' Label 'MANILA · SEPT 2026 · CUSTOMS', sub '20 towels + 20 duvets · suspected liquid meth'.

The boxes were flagged by X-ray screening after suspicious images were detected, which led to an Alert Order and a 100 percent physical examination. Narration (gotcha): 'The X-ray flagged the boxes.' Label 'X-RAY FLAG · THEN A FULL SEARCH', sub 'Declared as personal effects (BOC)'.

December 2015, Valencia, Spain: a shipping container from Colombia (arrived 30 November) held 40 pallets made of compressed cocaine made to look like wood: 1.4 tonnes (AFP, BBC); the UK National Crime Agency gave 1.5 tonnes, DC Velocity about 3,300 lb. Narration: 'The biggest? Shipping pallets made of cocaine.' Label 'VALENCIA, SPAIN · DEC 2015', sub 'A container from Colombia'.

FUN FACT: the container was declared as charcoal on wooden pallets, and some of its charcoal sacks also held cocaine disguised as charcoal; police suspected a charcoal company was a front for a lab that extracted the cocaine. Card 'SAME CONTAINER: / SOME OF THE CHARCOAL / WAS COCAINE TOO'.

Police acted on intelligence (DC Velocity: police intelligence and sniffer dogs; The National: intelligence from the UK National Crime Agency), and a forensic examination found the pallets were made of compressed cocaine powder made to look like wood. Narration (gotcha): 'On a tip, lab tests found the wood was cocaine.'
STATISTIC (counter 1,400 KG): the weight of the cocaine pallets as Spanish police gave it (AFP; BBC); the NCA's figure was 1.5 tonnes. Counter '1,400 KG' with the label 'PALLETS MADE OF COCAINE'.

The operation led to 11-12 arrests (sources differ) in Spain, Britain and Dubai, including two Colombian chemistry specialists per AFP. Nobody is named or drawn. Label 'ARRESTS IN SPAIN, BRITAIN, DUBAI'.

Neck pillows were among the clothes-shaped items made from the cocaine-silicone mix in the Kathmandu case. Narration (callback): 'Even the neck pillow was cocaine.' Callout 'NECK PILLOW · COCAINE + SILICONE'.
